scenarios.label: bull
conditions: Gross margin snaps back toward FY25 levels as new data-center capacity reaches full contracted revenue
All four named >$8bn AI-infrastructure customers (AMD, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, TikTok, xAI) keep converting RPO on or ahead of schedule with no pullback

scenarios.joint_probability_basis: A conjunction of three conditions (margin recovery AND customer follow-through AND multiple re-rating) must hold together for the $212.67 level; this is why Bull is weighted below Bear-cyclical, which needs only one adverse event (CLAUDE.md §10 conjunction check).

scenarios.label: base
conditions: Consensus NTM EBITDA ($49,996M) is roughly achieved

The market continues pricing Oracle's leverage (4.46x net debt/EBITDA) and eroding return on capital at a discount to its own recent multiple and to peers, with no further de-rating but no re-rating either
scenarios.joint_probability_basis: Both clauses describe the same 'no material change from today's pricing dynamic' condition, not two independent bets.

scenarios.label: bear_cyclical
conditions: At least one of the four named >$8bn AI-infrastructure customers pulls back materially on contracted RPO
The FY27 gross-margin step-down management has already flagged qualitatively lands harder than guided
scenarios.joint_probability_basis: The $94.62 target combines both a customer-concentration pullback and a further margin step-down in the same NTM EBITDA calculation; in practice either alone would pressure the stock, but the modeled target reflects both landing together.

scenarios.label: bear_structural
conditions: The confirmed-eroding moat trajectory (return on capital 12.35%→8.22% over four straight years) does not stabilize: OCI never develops AWS/Azure-level scale or switching-cost economics and becomes a fully commoditized, price-competed infrastructure line with no margin protection
The legacy software-support annuity (the one part of the business with a real, evidenced moat) keeps shrinking as a share of revenue faster than OCI can build a comparable-margin replacement
scenarios.joint_probability_basis: Both describe the same multi-year structural-reset path (the moat module's confirmed 'eroding' trajectory continuing to its logical endpoint), not two independent risks. This is a 24–36 month fundamental path; the price target is used here as the level the market could reprice toward within the 12-month scenario horizon once the reset becomes evident, not as proof the fundamentals fully resolve within 12 months — stated explicitly as a synthesizer judgment, not a module finding.

rating_cap: Watchlist ceiling — management-governance RF-MGT-005 (Critical, unresolved securities class action alleging Oracle overstated the AI-deal growth outlook) mechanically caps the rating at no better than Watchlist per CLAUDE.md §24 Filter 1, independently confirmed by valuation's negative margin of safety (-15.08%) and balance-sheet-survival's 'Stretched' solvency verdict.
variant_perception_summary: The consensus view is that Oracle's AI-infrastructure buildout (RPO +363% to $638bn, 97.5% GPU utilization) validates a premium multiple. What the current $153.94 price actually requires — a 51.3% FY2027 revenue beat against management's own freshly issued +33.6% guidance, and a 61.9% terminal EBIT margin no named peer has ever posted — is not what most narratives around the stock are pricing explicitly; it is a specific, testable, and currently unmet bar. Combined with a balance sheet where the real constraint (the ~$70bn FY2027 capex program, not the covenant or the maturity wall) breaks at just a 2%–20% EBITDA decline, and an unresolved securities-fraud allegation naming the founder and both co-CEOs, the setup is priced for a cleaner execution path than the evidence currently supports.
what_everyone_knows: Oracle is growing fast on AI-infrastructure demand (OCI +77% FY26, RPO +363% to $638bn) and is one of the named hyperscale-adjacent AI-capex beneficiaries alongside Microsoft and Amazon.
what_is_priced_in: A continuation of hyper-growth: the reverse-DCF shows today's price already assumes a 22.6% FY26-34 revenue CAGR, a 51.3% FY27 print (18 points above guidance), and a 61.9% terminal EBIT margin (best peer, Microsoft, is 46.8%).
what_market_may_be_missing: That the market-implied growth and margin path is quantifiably ahead of both management's own guidance and any peer precedent, at the same time the balance sheet's real fragility point (liquidity for the capex program, not debt service) sits inside normal-recession range, and that the same fiscal year carries two Critical governance red flags (unresolved securities-fraud allegation; dividend/capex not covered by free cash flow) that independently cap conviction regardless of the valuation call.
edge_proof: If Oracle's FQ1 FY2027 print (2026-09-04) shows revenue growth materially above the guided 27-29% CC/USD range with gross margin not stepping down further — converging toward the 51.3% YoY pace and 61.9% terminal margin the current price already requires — the overvaluation call is wrong and should be dropped. If growth instead lands within or below the guided range and/or gross margin compresses further as management has already flagged, the overvaluation call is confirmed.
killer_risk: A pullback, delay, or renegotiation by one of the four named >$8bn AI-infrastructure customers (AMD, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, TikTok, xAI) inside the $638bn RPO backlog, which would hit revenue directly while $167.4bn of debt-funded data-center capacity built to serve that demand stays on the books — compounding with a ~$70bn FY2027 capex program that a downside-stress test shows exhausts committed liquidity at just a 2%–20% EBITDA decline.
kill_criteria: FQ1 FY2027 revenue growth (reported 2026-09-04) prints below the guided 27-29% CC/USD range, or gross margin steps down materially more than management has already flagged — confirms the overvaluation and margin-timing-lag risk.
Any of the four named >$8bn AI-infrastructure customers pulls back, delays, or renegotiates contracted RPO — the single named killer risk across the earnings and business-model modules.

Committed liquidity is drawn down faster than the module's 2%-20% EBITDA-decline break point (e.g. the revolver is drawn, or a capex cut/fresh unsecured issuance is forced) — confirms balance-sheet-survival's 'Stretched' read.

The OCI securities class action (RF-MGT-005) survives the motion-to-dismiss stage (defendants respond by 2026-09-16; a ruling could land as late as ~2026-12-18) or is amended with stronger factual allegations — confirms the unresolved integrity signal.
